committee: CC Affordable Housing Trust Fund Board
overview: The CC Affordable Housing Trust Fund Board operates as a municipal trust and housing bank in Medford, Massachusetts, managing affordable housing policy, project funding allocations, and local revenue strategies. The board held 21 meetings across the 2024-2025 and 2026-2027 terms, spanning from August 7, 2024, to November 4, 2026. Over this duration, the board executed its legal Declaration of Trust, finalized a five-year affordable housing action plan, and developed standardized funding application procedures for housing developers. The board also collaborated on municipal zoning reforms, including fractional cash-in-lieu payment rules and an affordable housing linkage fee nexus study. At its November 4, 2026 meeting, the board elected its officer slate, reviewed quarterly financial reports showing $376,129 in unencumbered cash, approved a standardized developer application template, and canceled its scheduled December meeting.

threads.name: Declaration of Trust and board governance
threads.summary: In its initial meetings, the board formed working groups to draft a foundational Declaration of Trust and establish officer roles. Trustees reviewed draft governing procedures, including trustee removal rules and land disposition oversight, throughout late 2024. Board members officially executed and notarized the Declaration of Trust in January 2025 to enable recording at the Registry of Deeds. Later governance updates established quarterly financial reporting protocols and annual officer election schedules.

threads.name: Five-Year Affordable Housing Action Plan
threads.summary: The board initiated a multi-phase action plan process in late 2024, forming a subcommittee to oversee data collection and community engagement. Throughout early 2025, trustees reviewed demographic data, held focus groups with housing stakeholders, and hosted public listening workshops. A draft five-year action plan outlining goals for affordable housing creation, preservation, and revenue expansion was presented to the public in July 2025. The board formally approved the final five-year action plan in October 2025 and subsequently presented it to the City Council.

threads.name: Developer funding guidelines and application templates
threads.summary: To process incoming developer inquiries, the board initiated the creation of formal funding guidelines and loan document templates in early 2025. Trustees approved initial developer application guidelines and a draft Notice of Funding Availability, while exploring a transition to rolling funding applications. In 2026, the board revised project cost categories and operating budget requirements to create a standardized application template. The board formally approved the developer funding application template in November 2026 subject to minor AMI alignment adjustments.

threads.name: Funding for 703 Fellsway West project
threads.summary: In August 2025, Metro Community Housing requested $200,000 in funding for utility delays and cost overruns on a 3-unit project at 703 Fellsway West. The board reviewed loan terms for a $100,000 loan commitment in late 2025 and noted the issuance of certificates of occupancy. In April 2026, the board approved the $100,000 loan to cover soft costs and overruns. However, staff reported in May 2026 that original loan documents had not been recorded at the Registry of Deeds, prompting legal review before disbursing funds.

threads.name: Community Preservation Act funding and trust revenue
threads.summary: The board secured an initial $250,000 seed appropriation of Community Preservation Act funds following City Council approval in early 2025. Trustees regularly petitioned the Community Preservation Committee for additional allocations, securing $550,000 in FY26 funding. The board also established a fundraising working group to evaluate alternative revenue mechanisms, including real estate transfer fees, tax bill check-offs, and institutional payments. By late 2026, the board prepared its FY27 funding request presentation to the Community Preservation Committee.

threads.name: Inclusionary zoning fractional payments and incentive rules
threads.summary: The board began reviewing proposed municipal zoning amendments in late 2025, supporting a resolution for developers to make fractional cash payments in lieu of building full affordable units. Trustees submitted formal letters of support to the City Council while refining fee calculation formulas as state underlying metrics changed. The fractional payment ordinance formally took effect in late 2026. Concurrently, the board continued tracking the Community Development Board's review of affordable housing incentive bonus tables across rezoned districts.

threads.name: Affordable housing linkage fees and nexus study
threads.summary: The board identified housing linkage fees on commercial development as a core long-term funding source in late 2024. To satisfy statutory requirements, the board supported selling municipal land on McCormick Avenue to fund a mandatory nexus study. The city commissioned consultant Carl Seidman to conduct the linkage nexus study in early 2026. Following the study's completion, the City Council drafted linkage fee ordinance language and referred the proposal to the Community Development Board.
